deals.date_text: Agreement announced 28 December 2018; operating rights from January 2019
deals.evidence: reached a deal with MLS to take over operating rights of the Crew for a fee of $150 million
deals.headline: Haslam and Edwards families take over the Crew for a $150 million fee
deals.investor: Haslam Sports Group (Jimmy and Dee Haslam) and the Edwards family
deals.seller: Major League Soccer (operating rights previously held by Precourt Sports Ventures)
deals.summary: After Anthony Precourt's Precourt Sports Ventures moved its MLS rights to Austin, MLS agreed with the Haslam and Edwards families that they would take over the Crew's operating rights from January 2019, alongside a public-private partnership for a downtown stadium; Sportico reports the fee as $150 million.

deals.date_text: Public-private partnership approved December 2018; stadium opened July 2021
deals.evidence: Lower.com Field opened in July 2021 at a cost of $314 million, including $217.5 million in private funding.
deals.headline: Downtown stadium (now ScottsMiracle-Gro Field) built for $314 million, $217.5 million privately funded
deals.investor: Crew ownership (Haslam and Edwards families) with the City of Columbus, Franklin County and the State of Ohio
deals.summary: The downtown stadium, opened in July 2021 as Lower.com Field and renamed ScottsMiracle-Gro Field from 2026, cost $314 million including $217.5 million in private funding; the remainder came from the public partners in the 2018 public-private partnership.

deals.evidence: The MLS team was valued at $900 million in the transaction
deals.headline: Haslam Sports Group sells 10% of the Crew to the Edwards family at a $900 million valuation
deals.summary: HSG sold 10% to existing partner the Edwards family, taking the Edwards to 30% and HSG to 70%; Sportico reported the $900 million valuation from a person familiar with the agreement.

deals.date_text: Agreement reported 28 May 2026; Nationwide announced it had joined the ownership group on 25 June 2026
deals.evidence: Nationwide is buying a 30% stake in the Crew from Jimmy and Dee Haslam and 7% from the Edwards
deals.headline: Nationwide buys 37% of the Columbus Crew at a $900 million valuation
deals.seller: Haslam Sports Group (30%) and the Edwards family (7%)
deals.summary: Columbus-based insurer Nationwide, the Crew's jersey partner, bought 30% from Jimmy and Dee Haslam and 7% from the Edwards family at a $900 million valuation (Sportico, citing multiple people familiar with the details); the Haslams stay control owners at 40%. Nationwide's own release calls it a 'meaningful minority stake' and released no other terms. The same three parties are behind Columbus's NWSL expansion team, due to start in 2028.

deals.evidence: highlighted by a multi-year agreement for stadium naming rights
deals.headline: ScottsMiracle-Gro takes stadium naming rights from 2026
deals.summary: Multi-year naming rights agreement renaming Lower.com Field as ScottsMiracle-Gro Field from the 2026 season; terms not disclosed; negotiated with Legends Global.

founded_evidence: it all started in 1994 when it was announced that Columbus would be awarded Major League Soccer
name: Columbus Crew
notes: US clubs publish no accounts: revenue and operating income are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season (operating income is EBITDA as Forbes defines it), cited from the Wayback Machine copy because forbes.com refuses automated fetches; Sportico separately estimates 2025 revenue at $93 million. Forbes' $805 million is a hypothetical control value; the 2025 and 2026 stake sales were struck at $900 million. Founded year is when Columbus was announced as MLS's first franchise (1994); the first season was 1996. The Edwards family's holding after selling 7% to Nationwide is not stated on any page read (it was 30% after July 2025). Stadium owner not established: the Columbus Dispatch reported in 2022 that the Crew negotiated a purchase option on the stadium, implying public ownership, but dispatch.com could not be read. Not found: legal entity, average attendance, wages, social follower counts with a stated date.

ownership_summary: Haslam Sports Group (Jimmy and Dee Haslam, with Whitney and JW Johnson; owners of the NFL's Cleveland Browns) and the Columbus-based Edwards family (Dr. Pete Edwards) took over the Crew's operating rights from January 2019 for a $150 million fee. In July 2025 HSG sold 10% to the Edwards family at a $900 million valuation (HSG 70%, Edwards 30%). In 2026 Nationwide Mutual Insurance bought 37% (30% from the Haslams, 7% from the Edwards) at a $900 million valuation; the Haslams remain control owners and largest stakeholders at 40%.
